summary: A technical analysis of market cycles affecting GameStop, focusing on Supplementary Liquidity Deposit (SLD) cycles, C+21/C+35 calendar cycles, and alleged DTCC/NSCC vulnerabilities. The author attempts to decode DTCC settlement mechanics to predict GME price movements and speculates about mechanisms to hide fails-to-deliver. The document suggests RC could trigger a forced short squeeze through corporate events or NFT technology. Despite beginning with factual regulatory processes, it pivots to increasingly speculative claims, with the author themselves rating C+21 as ineffective and admitting major claims lack verification.

key_claims.claim: Claims that SLD cycles tied to monthly option expirations reliably correlate with measurable price movements in GME
key_claims.note: SLD cycles are real regulatory processes (page 3-10). However, the document provides no statistical validation, and hindsight shows these cycles did not reliably predict GME price movements after Aug 2021.

key_claims.claim: Claims that C+21 calendar cycles predict GME price movement
key_claims.note: Author explicitly states on page 40-41: 'C+21 used to have an effect on GME, but not anymore. It's not a decent price mover.' and 'At this point C+21 is in fact mostly horse shit.' Prediction failed.

key_claims.claim: Claims that C+35 calendar cycles effectively predict GME price movements
key_claims.note: Author rates C+35 at only 4.5/10 confidence (page 40) and later concludes (page 48): 'Nothing special to look forward to' and 'C+ cycles used to have a decent impact...at this point their effects on the underlying price are close to invisible.' Prediction collapsed.

key_claims.claim: Claims that fails-to-deliver can be hidden via One Day Settling (ODS) exemptions and Obligation Warehouse mechanics, preventing detection of naked shorts
key_claims.note: Author includes 'Big Fucking Warning' (page 14) stating: 'the whole part about not appearing as a fail if you don't pass through CNS is not 100% verified.' Unsubstantiated speculation lacking primary verification.

key_claims.claim: Claims that RC can trigger a forced short squeeze (MOASS) by executing a corporate reorganization (stock split, merger) because X-REORG exemptions will be forced to close
key_claims.note: GameStop executed a 4-for-1 stock split (July 2022) and launched an NFT marketplace (2022). Neither triggered a squeeze or forced covering. No MOASS occurred. Prediction failed.

key_claims.claim: Claims that the Robinhood margin call on January 28, 2021 was triggered by the coincidence of a bank holiday disrupting SLD settlement cycles
key_claims.note: SEC October 2021 report concluded the Jan 2021 run-up was driven by positive retail sentiment, not margin mechanics or short covering. Causal claim unsupported by official findings.

key_claims.claim: Claims that DTCC/NSCC infrastructure runs on legacy IBM systems with unaddressed vulnerabilities that could enable hiding of fails-to-deliver
key_claims.note: Author explicitly states (page 53): 'Don't ask me for source. I can't give you shit.' Conjecture based on reading public documents without evidence of actual exploitable vulnerabilities.

key_claims.claim: Claims that stacking multiple overlapping C+21 and C+35 cycles produces amplified price movements
key_claims.note: Author tested this and reported (page 48-49): 'I've already studied what overlaps with many C+'s and SLD cycles does. It does fuck all. It used to. Not anymore.' Empirically failed.

validity_rationale: The document correctly describes real DTCC settlement processes (SLD cycles, CNS netting, FTD mechanics) and accurately explains regulatory terminology. However, its core thesis—that these cycles predictably move GME's price and that hidden MOASS-triggering vulnerabilities exist in the DTCC—is contradicted by hindsight. The author themselves admits C+21 no longer works and C+35 is unreliable (giving it 4.5/10 confidence). GameStop later executed the speculated corporate events (stock split, NFT platform) without triggering forced short covering. Most critically, the document makes unverified claims about DTCC vulnerabilities with explicit warnings of lacking proof. Speculation dominates the second half (pages 14-18).
